### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **5** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/plugin-hono-server`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **43** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **4** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/security.json`, `packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/permission.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**7** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx`  _(via validateRlsPredicateEnforceability (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/permissions/field-level-security.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/permissions/index.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via canWriteObject (symbol, a top-level function), registerAuthzMiddleware (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/plugins/packages.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectql/security.mdx`  _(via FieldPermissionSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/ui/forms.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **4** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/implementation-status.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via FieldPermissionSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via canWriteObject (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-0.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **4** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/security.json`, `packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/permission.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **154** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0479cd6a0a6abb77b8180f7cf14e5eda778cce42` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b0c06d7c3b53aefa701b45c388951b0696b11f13` — the merge of head `3d3775861b6d3c6dbf87402fbe71d64703127399` into base `0479cd6a0a6abb77b8180f7cf14e5eda778cce42`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b0c06d7c3b53aefa701b45c388951b0696b11f13 && git checkout b0c06d7c3b53aefa701b45c388951b0696b11f13
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 0479cd6a0a6abb77b8180f7cf14e5eda778cce42 3d3775861b6d3c6dbf87402fbe71d64703127399 && git checkout -B drift-repro 0479cd6a0a6abb77b8180f7cf14e5eda778cce42 && git merge --no-ff 3d3775861b6d3c6dbf87402fbe71d64703127399

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0479cd6a0a6abb77b8180f7cf14e5eda778cce42
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 0479cd6a0a6abb77b8180f7cf14e5eda778cce42` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `3d3775861b6d3c6dbf87402fbe71d64703127399`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/security/permission.zod.ts, docs/adr/0066-unified-authorization-model.md + packages/core/src/security/effective-object-permissions.ts, packages/core/src/security/index.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/permission-evaluator.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/rls-compiler.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-object-inputs.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-object-admission.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/explain-engine.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-rls-predicate-enforceability.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/current-user-endpoints.ts, packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json, .changeset/25866-field-permission-row-condition.md, and the five test files of the diff. Read in the cited code at the head, unchanged by the diff: security-plugin-addressed-writes.ts (`extractSingleId`, `readRowById`), security-plugin.ts (`getCallerPreImage`), rls-check-stored-form.ts (`storedFormCheckJudge`), field-masker.ts (`detectForbiddenWrites`), rls-compiler.ts (`compileExpressionOutcome`, `judgeCompiledComparands`, `compileFilter`), packages/lint/src/authoring-rules.ts (the rule's registration), packages/spec/src/shared/refinement-projection.ts and strict-object.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/runtime-authoring-gate.ts, and ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/PermissionMatrixEditor.tsx (the Studio form the ruling names). The rest of the diff (the generated reference pages, authorable surface, liveness ledger and state count, and the three hand-written doc pages) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at TIER_DEFAULT.

Inputs: card #25866 (body and all six comments: ruling 6408558941 letter A, premise check 6409890004, Claim 6410022810, os-dev-report 6411406490), PR #25980 (body, 28-file list, net diff against main from merge-base 38050ced7: +1132 / -96), and the 55 check-runs on the head: 46 success, 9 skipped (opt-in harnesses and matrix placeholders), 0 failure, 0 pending at the time of this record; all eight required contexts success. PR state while reviewing: open, not merged, approved by os-zhuang (review 5648858472 on 94d1fde6, not dismissed), auto-merge armed by os-zhuang.

### ① Derived judgments

1. Accept-set widening, `FieldPermissionSchema.when` (right). An optional non-blank string on the strict object; `condition` / `where` / `filter` refused with a pointer to `when`; blank and null refused with the stated prescription. The test file pins each of these and the ride on `PermissionSetSchema.fields` (`z.record(z.string(), FieldPermissionSchema)`, so the refinement runs on every set entry) and on `GetObjectPermissionsResponse.fieldPermissions`, which reuses the same schema.
2. Edit vote only, refused at parse beside `readable: false` (right). The object refinement `p.when === undefined || p.readable !== false` issues at path `when` with the message naming the EDIT vote. This is exactly the ruling's part ① (a `when` on `readable` refused at parse and the spec says so). The refinement cannot project: the closed list in refinement-projection.ts has `requiredOneOf`, `dependentRequired` (presence only; its own docblock excludes the if/then form), `bannedKeys`, `bannedKeyPattern` and `NON_BLANK_STRING` (which the `when` value uses, so that half does project). The seven new ledger rows in dropped-refinements.baseline.json are all positions where FieldPermission is embedded (the root site plus `fields.valueType` / `fieldPermissions.valueType` under PermissionSet, the manifest unions and GetObjectPermissionsResponse); none is laundered pre-existing drift, and the published JSON Schema states the rule in `when`'s description as the ledger requires.
3. Runtime honours the key as the describe text and the ADR note say (right). `fieldPermissionVote` (core) is the one reading: no `when` votes bits `=== true` under every verdict; `unmatched` is absent (null, no vote); `unjudged` keeps the read bit and withholds the edit grant. `PermissionEvaluator.getFieldPermissions(object, sets, judge?)` votes through it; with no judge every conditioned entry is `unjudged`. Pinned in the evaluator battery, including the sibling-grant union: a matched conditioned lock is out-voted by an unconditioned `editable: true`, which is the ADR-0066 ⑧ posture unchanged.
4. Which row, judged in process, never the using gate's query rewrite (right). `computeForbiddenFieldWrites` (now async, with a `row` argument) takes the fast path when no set carries a `when` for the object. Otherwise each distinct `when` is compiled once by `RLSCompiler.compileRowPredicate` (the same `compileExpressionOutcome`, the extracted `userContextOf` with its reserved-key refusal, `judgeCompiledFields` under the object's field guard and `judgeCompiledComparands` in the `check` position; no OR-combination, no deny sentinel) and judged by `storedFormCheckJudge([filter], writeCheckFieldOptions(object))` over `matchesFilterCondition`. An insert is judged on each incoming row of the payload on its own values, the union refused; a by-id update on the memoised caller-context pre-image (`getCallerPreImage(opCtx, extractSingleId(opCtx))`, the same read steps 2.7 and 2.8 share, fetched through a thunk only when a `when` exists). The `ql.findOne` rewrite at authz-middleware ~1030 is not reached from this path. The middleware battery pins: draft insert admitted / approved insert refused / bulk union; stored approved row refused even when the payload moves to draft; stored draft row admitted even when the payload approves; exactly one by-id caller-context `findOne`.
5. Fail-closed, lock and never a silent grant (right). A null pre-image (absent or invisible to the caller), a predicate update (`extractSingleId` null), a reader with no `preImage` thunk (`canWriteObject` on update), a predicate that yields no filter (unresolved `current_user.*`, undeclared column, refused comparand) and a judge that throws (the JSON-column refusal `storedFormCheckJudge` raises) each resolve to `unjudged`, so the entry contributes no edit grant, and each path emits a `[Security]` WARN naming the cause. In code order step 2.7 runs before step 2.5, so a null pre-image on a by-id update is answered 404 at 2.7 first; the field gate's own null-pre-image lock is pinned directly on the derivation, and the predicate-update lock and the `current_user.nope` lock are pinned through the middleware. No path returns an empty forbidden list for a conditioned entry without judging the row.
6. Most-permissive merge across sets, row-blind readers report the lock (right). `buildEffectiveFieldPermissions` (core, new) merges `fieldPermissionVote(entry, 'unjudged')` across sets with fresh entries, and `/auth/me/permissions` now calls it instead of its inline copy, which would have advertised a conditioned grant as editable. The other readers of `getFieldPermissions` (explain-access mask, field-readers projection, query-guard perms, result masker) pass no judge and are unchanged, so each applies the lock; the explain `fls` layer additionally names each row-conditioned entry (`conditionedFieldEntries`), pinned in the explain test. No in-repo caller pre-gates an engine update with `canWriteObject(update, data)` (zero non-test call sites outside plugin-security), so its always-lock answer on update narrows nothing the card measured.
7. Lint, validated like an RLS predicate at authoring and publish (right). `permissions[].fields[key].when` is walked by `judgeClause(graph, source, 'when', site, undefined, membership)` against the key's object (the head before the first dot): the shape pass (`isSupportedRlsExpression`, the same predicate `compileFilter` consults), the reference pass (unknown field, unknown user variable, cross-object) and the list-holding / cross-class comparand verdicts all run; the engine `judgeFilter` is withheld exactly as it is for `check` (it is read-scope `using` only), so `when` is judged as a `check` is. The rule is registered `commands: ALL`, `surfaces: CLI_AND_RUNTIME`, `runtimeTypes: ['permission', 'object']`, so it reaches `os validate` / `os lint` and the runtime publish gate for permission writes: the describe text's "authoring and publish time" holds. The four injections, the path / where / cost text, the key-object targeting and the blank skip are pinned.
8. Bits now read `=== true` where the evaluator read truthiness (right, noted). For a parsed entry the two are identical (schema defaults materialise booleans); for a malformed stored entry carrying a non-boolean truthy value the new reading is narrower, which is the fail-closed direction and the contract-first one (such an entry is refused at parse). Not byte-identical in the strict sense the PR body claims, but never wider.
9. An insert is judged on the payload as sent (right per the ruling, noted). A conditioned column absent from the incoming row is `unmatched`, so a lock on `status in [...]` does not bite on an insert that omits `status` and relies on a default the engine applies later. The ruling says "on create, the incoming row" and the describe text says "as the caller sent it", so the runtime matches the contract; if a consuming app needs defaults consulted, that is a later widening with its own card, not a defect here.
10. ADR-0066 ⑧ note (right, one prose defect). The note records the narrowing-where-it-votes semantics, the union-without-deny posture unchanged, the judged row, the fail-closed lock and the authoring validation, each matching the code above. Its last sentence is garbled: "The muting/deny layer ⑦ still owes remains the mechanism for taking an edit away that another set grants." reads as two drafts merged. The meaning (⑦ remains the mechanism for taking an edit away) is recoverable and reverses nothing, so it is not a contract fault; it owes a docs-only follow-up PR on the ADR, not a push onto this head.
11. Public surface (right). core exports `buildEffectiveFieldPermissions`, `fieldPermissionVote` and three types; plugin-security adds `RLSCompiler.compileRowPredicate`, exports `RlsDropCause` and `RlsRowPredicateOutcome`, widens `getFieldPermissions` with an optional third argument and adds `conditionedFieldEntries` (the changed `computeForbiddenFieldWrites` is private); `authorable-surface/security.json` gains `security/FieldPermission:when`; liveness classifies `fields.when` live with its readers. All widenings; nothing removed or renamed, no tombstone owed.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/25866-field-permission-row-condition.md` declares `minor` on `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/lint` and `@objectstack/plugin-hono-server`, which are exactly the five published packages the diff moves. The two declaration lines read `yes (widening)` for Clause-② and `added` for Metadata-protocol in both the PR body and the changeset body, and both are right: a new authorable key is `added`, the kind takes at least `minor` on every moved package, and `(widening)` is the correct arm for a key that refuses nothing previously accepted. No `skip-changeset`; `Check Changeset` is success on the head. The ruling's "minor on @objectstack/spec" is met.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Deviation 1 (lint landed in validate-rls-predicate-enforceability.ts, not validate-security-posture.ts): answered, right. That rule owns the compiler-backed passes and the five `rls-predicate-*` ids; a second spelling would be the drift it exists to prevent. validate-security-posture.ts reads key qualification and field existence only, which `when` does not change.
- Deviation 2 (plugin-hono-server touched): answered, right. The endpoint carried an inline copy of the field merge; left alone it would have reported a conditioned grant as editable to the console, a reading wider than the gate.
- Deviation 3 (generated spec artefacts beyond json-schema) and deviation 4 (three hand-written doc pages): answered, right. All are the Claim's "+ generated spec artefacts" or hand-written trees AGENTS.md leaves editable; no release-owned page is touched, and the Docs Drift Check named the three pages.
- Not measured, hotclm#126/#127 (the ruling's premise (c)): escalated as acceptable. The seat cannot read that repository; the premise check 6409890004 located the row-blind denial in code (`computeForbiddenFieldWrites` from authz-middleware ~1194) and the tests use the card's exact shape. Re-measurement on hotclm belongs to the hotclm#127 unblock, which the ruling ties to a published release.
- Not measured, Studio form: ESCALATED, the dev's premise is wrong and the ruling's clause is undelivered. The dev wrote that `../objectui` is unreadable and that the form's key offer is the schema's. The Console source is in this tree under `ui/`, and `ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/PermissionMatrixEditor.tsx` is a hand-written matrix of two checkboxes (`readable`, `editable`) with no `when` input and no display of an authored one. Measured consequences: a per-field toggle spreads the entry (`{ ...cur, [action]: value }`) so an authored `when` survives; the bulk `readable` / `writable` shortcuts rewrite the entry as two booleans and drop it (the `writable` case turns a conditioned lock into an unconditioned grant, by an explicit admin act on those fields, not silently); and the readable-off cascade produces `readable: false` beside a `when`, which the spec now refuses at the publish gate, so that save fails loudly with no way in the form to clear the condition. Nothing here widens the runtime gate, and the PR never claims the form, so it does not fail this contract; but ruling 6408558941 part ① names "the Studio permission-set form offers the key" and this PR closes the card with `Fixes #25866`. The owning seat should file the Studio form as its own card in the ui lane (offer `when`, show an authored one, keep it across the bulk shortcuts, and make the readable-off cascade clear it) before or at the close of #25866, and correct the "Not measured" paragraph of the PR body so the record does not state a false premise.
- Earlier reds on 94d1fde6 and 46400bf0: explained by the dev as lanes cancelled by the next push; on the reviewed head every gate-carrying context is success, which is the only reading this record relies on.
- Landing: Tier H (docs/adr). os-zhuang's approval (5648858472) stands on an earlier commit and is not dismissed; auto-merge was armed by os-zhuang, none of it a seat write. Nothing in this record asks for a push onto this head: the one prose defect (①.10) and the Studio gap are follow-ups.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-xnz0xa`
Reviewed-by: `session_01RyMY3prh9GRva1Tt37Di3i`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## 席位核对

REWORK (patch round, same thread) · domain:spec seat 2 · 2026-10-26T08:33Z · head `3d3775861b6d3c6dbf87402fbe71d64703127399`

The contract review on this head is PASS (comment 6411620876): the spec key, the in-process row judge, fail-closed locking, the merge and the semver all hold. The PR is incomplete against the ruling it closes, so it does not land as `Fixes #25866` yet.

1. **Studio form (ruling 6408558941 ①: "the Studio permission-set form offers the key").** Not delivered. The PR body's "Not measured" premise (Studio is `../objectui`, unreadable) is false: the console is in this tree under `ui/`. `ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/PermissionMatrixEditor.tsx` is a two-checkbox matrix with no `when` input or display. Its readable-off cascade can also produce `readable: false` beside an authored `when`, a shape this PR now refuses at publish, and the form gives the author no way to clear it. The patch must:
   - offer and show `when` on the edit vote;
   - keep the cascade and bulk shortcuts from producing the refused shape;
   - add tests.
2. **ADR-0066 ⑧ note.** Its last sentence is garbled ("The muting/deny layer ⑦ still owes remains the mechanism…"). Rewrite it.
3. **PR body.**
   - Replace the "Not measured" Studio paragraph.
   - Soften "byte-identical" for the evaluator: it now reads `=== true`, which is identical for parsed entries and fail-closed for malformed stored ones.

The claim's file surface is amended to include the form. After the push, the same-head contract review is re-run on the new head. The maintainer's approval needs a fresh look after the push.
